entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 executive order and foreign-ministry rule bar X markers and markers not matching assigned sex at birth; the 24 Feb 2025 cable orders refusal where document discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex and invites consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report passports confiscated or blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; the regime is actively litigated by a civil-liberties union; a legal-aid FAQ advises travellers on documentation.
entry_documents.interaction: State licence-X rescission and the state's tightening document climate compound friction, but the visitor's home passport governs at entry, so the federal cable is the operative rule.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Birth-sex custody placement documented in a peer state (trans woman held 24 hours in a men's ward after restroom arrest); from 2026 federal corrections policy mandates conversion-therapy-style regime (hair cutting, hormone removal); immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; several orders are enjoined; courts accept challenges.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any state-level arrest for facility use feeds directly into federal custody practices that are themselves hostile.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities; the state's 2023 school facility ban (extended 2025) plus Act 619's misdemeanour for public-bathroom use where a minor is present and intent is shown; four states criminalise in some circumstances; a documented arrest under a peer state's law with handcuffing and men's-ward holding.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Act 619 requires both willful entry and refusal to leave with a sexual-intent element, so arrest is not automatic; 29 state/provinces lack bans (climate signal only).
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding rules reach facilities regardless of the state map; whether this state's ban extends to general government buildings beyond schools is not stated.

care_services.exposure: A bill signed 26 March lets medical practitioners cite religious beliefs to deny healthcare to LGBT patients — directly reachable by a visitor seeking care; minors' care ban was allowed back into enforcement by the appeals circuit in Aug 2025 with litigation continuing; proposed federal rules would bar insurance reimbursement for under-18s.
care_services.protection: Care-ban litigation continues and a national judge previously enjoined it for irreparable harm; legal-aid resources exist.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces the care ban and religious-refusal layer simultaneously, though enforcement against visitors is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; Dec 2025 reward memo and 'radical gender ideology' framing; Jan 2025 order calling minors' care 'mutilation'; DOJ hospital-record subpoenas; 66% of the public supports ASAB listing on documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The dossier notes the reward criterion is not gender ideology and that counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; same-sex marriage and national employment protection remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both outing probability and the severity of any state encounter it colours.

minors_guardians.exposure: K-12 facility ban, trans-athlete ban, care ban in force pending litigation, religious care-denial statute, and a federal order directing investigation and prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; record subpoenas for under-19 patients.
minors_guardians.protection: Federal courts have enjoined parts of the care regime; legal-aid FAQ and ongoing litigation provide some cover.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor can be pushed into care denial, missed services or official inquiry; direct application of these measures to visiting families is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state hate-crime or civil-remedy coverage for gender identity (the 2021 hate-crimes act expressly excludes it) and no state anti-discrimination law; only the national hate-crime act and Bostock apply; advisories tell travellers to check recent violence reports.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime coverage since 2009 and functioning civil-rights litigation.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin state recourse makes police response after an incident unreliable; incident rates and patterns for visitors are not documented, so frequency is unknown.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: A July 2026 assessment places the state in 'Worst Policies In Effect', one tier below four 'Do Not Travel' states whose regimes include felony bathroom bans and bounty suits; Act 619's enforcement record is undocumented; multiple federal orders are in flux, so operative rules shift with travel dates.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation, an equality-map tracking regime, a legal-aid FAQ, and courts that have struck hostile measures (before later reversals) show institutions functioning.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Rule of law partially cuts both ways: the appeals circuit's Aug 2025 reversal shows efficient institutions can also enforce hostile policy.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.15-B: there is no routine secondary-inspection detention regime, no crowded-cell abuse, no withheld medical care in custody as border practice, and imprisonment for presentation is not the typical outcome. Entry refusal and document scrutiny are administrative, with litigation and consular advisories rather than months-long custody.

Close to 0.45-A: both show routine checkpoint exposure driven by document/presentation discrepancy, possible detention and humiliation, denial of care, narrow and slow remedies, and inconsistent enforcement. This dossier adds a care-denial statute and documented birth-sex ward placement, pulling slightly below the anchor.

Below 0.75-C: there trained border staff accept congruent documents with tribunal appeals and compensation. Here the operative cable instructs refusal on sex discrepancy with a possible lifetime fraud finding, and facility use carries misdemeanour exposure — no equivalent entry protection or compensation pathway is documented.

Well below 0.95-C: care cannot be refused there and inspectors enforce equity. Here practitioners may lawfully refuse LGBT care on religious grounds, facility use is restricted by federal and state rules, and remedies are contested. Social friction is not the issue; state-authored exclusions are.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is federal entry screening layered over a state ranked among the worst in force. Universal exposure sits at the border (refusal on sex discrepancy, possible lifetime fraud finding, marker rules) and in federally funded single-sex facilities. At state level a visitor faces conditional misdemeanour exposure for public-facility use, a religious care-denial statute, and no state discrimination or hate-crime recourse — while federal custody, if reached, imposes birth-sex placement and conversion-style policy. Mitigation is real but partial: functioning courts, active litigation, legal-aid guidance, national hate-crime coverage and no criminalisation of identity itself. Severity is arrest, ward misplacement and denied care rather than likely imprisonment, so the rating falls in the elevated band, not the high-risk tiers.
